item.text:
**Verdict**
Mixed, leaning no. In 2024 there was clear stabilization intent and some concrete reform action under IMF pressure, but the macro picture remained fragile: inflation was high, reserves were under strain, the taka was under pressure, and several major investment choices looked politically distorted rather than productivity-driven.

**Accepted Claims**
- [Bangladesh: Second Reviews Under the ECF/EFF and RSF Arrangements](https://www.elibrary.imf.org/view/journals/002/2024/186/article-A001-en.xml) — IMF, June 24, 2024.  
  Claim: The IMF said Bangladesh’s program performance was broadly on track and that the authorities had realigned the exchange rate, adopted a crawling peg, tightened monetary policy, and pursued tax/subsidy reforms to safeguard macro stability. This is the strongest positive evidence that the government was trying to protect macro stability and fiscal/monetary credibility.  
  Question IDs: `5B.3`

- [IMF reaches staff-level agreement on the second review of Bangladesh’s ECF/EFF and RSF](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/05/07/pr-24141-bangladesh-agreement-on-ecf-eff-and-rsf-arrangements) — IMF, May 7, 2024.  
  Claim: IMF staff said Bangladesh had adopted critical reforms, including exchange-rate realignment, a crawling peg, and liberalization of retail interest rates, and urged continued tightening plus revenue-based consolidation. That is real stabilization policy, but it was still clearly a repair effort in response to macro imbalances.  
  Question IDs: `5B.3`

- [Bangladesh: remarkable development progress](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099514001022413953) — World Bank, December 31, 2023, disclosed January 2, 2024.  
  Claim: Bangladesh entered 2024 with substantial development gains already in place, which is background evidence that the state had some capacity for long-run development. It does not prove 2024 macro stewardship, but it is the best positive baseline context.  
  Question IDs: `5B.3`, also `5B.1`

- [Financial Sector and Fiscal Policy Reforms Will Help Bangladesh Sustain Strong Growth](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/04/02/financial-sector-and-fiscal-policy-reforms-will-help-bangladesh-sustain-strong-growth-despite-strong-growth-south-asia-r) — World Bank, April 2, 2024.  
  Claim: The World Bank said Bangladesh faced high inflation, a persistent balance-of-payments deficit, financial-sector vulnerabilities, and pressure on FX reserves and the taka. This is strong negative evidence that macro stability was not being successfully protected.  
  Question IDs: `5B.3`

- [Factbox: Troubled Bangladesh’s economy bogged down by high unemployment, inflation](https://m.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/factboxtroubled-bangladeshs-economy-bogged-down-by-high-unemployment-inflation-3561503?ampMode=1) — Reuters, August 8, 2024.  
  Claim: Reuters summarized that under Hasina the current account deficit widened, the taka depreciated, reserves fell, inflation stayed near 10%, and Bangladesh needed an IMF bailout. That is direct evidence against a claim of strong macro stewardship in 2024.  
  Question IDs: `5B.3`

- [Bangladeshi nuclear prestige illusion](https://www.thedailystar.net/opinion/views/news/bangladeshs-nuclear-prestige-illusion-3590666) — The Daily Star, April 20, 2024.  
  Claim: The project was criticized as prestige-driven at a time of debt and inflation. This supports the view that long-term investment conditions were being distorted by political signaling, not optimized for broad economic returns.  
  Question IDs: `5B.3`, also `5B.1`

- [Rooppur Power Plant was AL govt's white elephant](https://www.tbsnews.net/bangladesh/energy/rooppur-power-plant-was-al-govts-white-elephant-energy-sector-experts-958801) — TBS News, October 5, 2024.  
  Claim: Energy-sector experts described Rooppur as a white-elephant project tied to mismanagement and corruption. That is negative evidence for long-term investment conditions and fiscal discipline.  
  Question IDs: `5B.3`, also `5B.1`, `5B.2`

**Search Gap**
- I found no reliable 2024 evidence that Hasina independently delivered durable macro stability. The strongest positives are IMF-backed corrective reforms, not proof of success.
- The best negative evidence is broader and more convincing: inflation, reserve pressure, currency weakness, and high-risk capital spending all remained serious problems.
